summary: Wallowa County, OR tower site on the Umatilla NF: a 1932 pole tower, an 1949 L-4 replacement, gone by 1987. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 87-foot treated-timber L-4 tower (1949), replacing a 48-foot pole tower (1932)
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umatilla National Forest
facts.status_note: Gone by 1987; no source describes what remains at the site today

events.note: Cabin built and first used at the site (register)
Newspaper item reports a tower of about 70 feet under construction, with a cabin on top; the height and date do not match the register
87-foot treated-timber L-4 tower replaced the 1932 pole tower
Old tower condemned and pulled down, per a Walla Walla Union-Bulletin item
Two Forest Service workers serving as lookouts (August 1953 newspaper item)
Lookout downgraded to a stand-by lookout

evidence.quote: First used with a cabin built in 1930, a 48' pole 7x7' tower was constructed in 1932.

evidence.supports: 1931 item: tower about 70 feet high under construction
evidence.quote: The forest service is building a lookout tower about 70 feet high at the Bone Springs ranger station 40 miles northeast of Tollgate, near the Skyline road reports the Leader.

evidence.supports: 1931 item: cabin on top of the tower
evidence.quote: these will be surmounted by a convenient cabin from which the forest fire lookout may make his observations

evidence.supports: replaced by an 87-foot treated-timber L-4 tower in 1949
evidence.quote: It was replaced by a 87' treated timber L-4 tower in 1949.
Both are over 80 feet in height with permanent living quarters at the top, like small pent-houses.

evidence.supports: old tower condemned and pulled down
evidence.quote: The former tower at Bone Springs was condemned a few weeks ago after serving for more than a quarter of a century.

evidence.supports: old tower pulled down about three weeks later
evidence.quote: Three weeks ago rangers and workers pulled it down.

evidence.supports: 1953 two Forest Service workers as lookouts

evidence.quote: The lookout was downgraded to a stand-by lookout.

corrections.why: The register gives an 87-foot (about 26.5 m) L-4 tower for 1949. The record's 24.4 m is 80 feet, the figure the 1949 newspaper gives as 'over 80 feet' (a lower bound). Editor to confirm which structure the record describes.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1949 newspaper's 'over 80 feet' is consistent with the register's 87-foot figure for the 1949 tower, since 80 feet is a lower bound.

notes_for_editor: The 1931 newspaper's 'about 70 feet' tower, the register's 48-foot 1932 pole tower and the 1930 cabin are not reconciled by any source read. The record's height_m of 24.4 may come from the 1949 newspaper's 80-foot figure; see corrections. Access is unknown and no source describes the site today, so the story gives no visit advice. Also not used: a 1929 road item and a 1936 item from the same Forest Lookouts page, which do not concern the lookout's structure. A separate Bone Point lookout (Whitman NF, about 40 feet high, per a 1946 NGS note on the same page) is a different site and is not used here.
